products.name: Exchange Online Mailbox Automation with Logic Apps Managed Identity — Replacing the O365 Connector with Microsoft Graph — Commercial
products.short_description: Your Logic App can't read a mailbox with a managed identity through the Office 365 connector — here's why, and the supported Microsoft Graph design that works with no stored service account.
products.description:
Your Logic App can't read a mailbox with a managed identity through the Office 365 connector — here's why, and the supported Microsoft Graph design that works with no stored service account.

Teams try to authenticate an Azure Logic Apps workflow to an Exchange Online mailbox with a system-assigned managed identity, using the Office 365 Outlook 'when a new email arrives' trigger — and hit a wall: that connector authenticates as a user/service account (OAuth), not as a managed identity, so the trigger cannot bind to the MI. This solution explains the root cause plainly, then rebuilds the workflow on Microsoft Graph: the Logic App uses its managed identity holding an application Graph permission to read the target mailbox, with the mailbox access scoped down so the identity can read exactly one mailbox and nothing else. It presents both supported alternatives — event-driven Graph change notifications and Graph polling — and helps you pick, then delivers a working, credential-free mailbox automation.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can follow end to end — backed by ready-to-run PowerShell.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps with full navigation paths; every object you create is named and reused through testing and troubleshooting.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; a comparable consulting engagement runs well into the thousands per day. Reusable on every rollout.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with explicit pass/fail gates.

What's inside

  • Root cause — why the Office 365 Outlook connector trigger cannot authenticate with a system-assigned managed identity (connector auth model vs MI), flagged verify-with-Microsoft
  • The supported Graph design — Logic App (system- or user-assigned MI) + application Graph permission reading the mailbox, no stored service-account connection
  • Choose your pattern — event-driven Graph change notifications vs Graph polling, with a decision table (points to the sibling products that go deep on each)
  • Least-privilege mailbox scoping — grant the identity read to ONE mailbox, not the tenant (cross-references the dedicated Graph-RBAC / Application Access Policy product)
  • Build + validate — the end-to-end Logic App, PowerShell readiness/validation scripts, and a test that proves the MI reads the mailbox and no other

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each deployment feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook for the next wave and the next project.

The bottom line

A working Exchange Online mailbox automation driven by a managed identity over Microsoft Graph — no service account, no stored secret, scoped to exactly the mailbox it needs.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as downloadable files you keep and reuse across unlimited devices — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF) — the complete, click-by-click solution: solution overview, requirements, step-by-step implementation, testing & validation, troubleshooting, best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run scripts (read-only discovery/validation/reporting; remediation defaults to a safe preview):
    • LAMIMAIL-Discovery.ps1 — read-only discovery of the Logic App managed identity, the application
    • LAMIMAIL-Report.ps1 — report the application-permission grants on the managed identity and the
    • LAMIMAIL-Set-AppRole.ps1 — assign (or verify/remove) the least-privilege APPLICATION Graph
    • LAMIMAIL-Test-MailboxAccess.ps1 — prove the security boundary: the identity can read the IN-scope
    • LAMIMAIL-Validate.ps1 — PASS/FAIL validation that the managed identity exists, holds ONLY the

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all five PowerShell scripts in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.
